findings.text: An embedded member of `items` breaks the whole items view: `Item.load()` returns the item itself when there is no file, not a Promise (public/framework/core/Item/Item.js:552), and `LiveItemsView` calls `item.load().then(...)` on every member (public/live/LivePage.js:524), so `{"items":{"add":{"title":"Note"}}}` throws a TypeError inside draw(). Fix: make `load()` always async (`Promise.resolve(this)`), or wrap the call in `Promise.resolve(...)` in the view. Item.test.mjs then checks `await embedded.load() === embedded`.

Ask 3 is not built: "the item tool also builds a loose /live/item-test/thing.jsonl as LivePage, inheriting from its folder's page.jsonl class". The diff makes no change to Servex/agents/page_tools.js. `class_of()` (page_tools.js:544) still returns "Page" for a file whose line 1 has no `class`, and thing.jsonl's line 1 is `{"title":"Thing"}`. The required item_tool test ("writing to /live/item-test/thing.jsonl replays it as LivePage") is also missing. The landing caveat says the class inheritance only needs a Servex restart, but no Servex code changed, so a restart would not fix it.

The proof is not in the task folder: shot-1/2/3 png exist only in the worktree and are not in the diff, and the probe's JSON output was never saved. Also, shot-2-after-tail.png stops at the "THING" heading, so it does not show the appended line arriving. Commit the shots and the probe output (`git add -f`), and shoot the tailed text in view.

Links to docs that do not exist: Page.class.js (items getter comment) and LivePage.js:150 cite `doc/jsonl.md "page.items"`, and Item.js file_url() cites `ids-and-paths.md, "page.items"`. core/Page/doc/jsonl.md has no page.items section, and there is no ids-and-paths.md anywhere. Add the short section to core/Page/doc/jsonl.md (`load_file`: the file url and the page's address passed separately) or point the comments at core/Item/readme.md.

There are two live objects for one file. The items card opens thing.jsonl through `Item.open` (Store.for), but the route /live/item-test/thing opens it through `LivePage.jsonl_file` → `Reader.for` (core/Page/Jsonl.js:35). So the "one object per url" dedup that load() promises does not cover the full-page route. It would be simpler to have `child()` reuse `stub.load()`, or to log why it can't.

/live/item-test/thing renders as an empty LivePage ("Nothing on screen yet.", shot-3-thing-route.png): the tailed `{text}` lines set a field the page never draws. The brief only asked for `.live-page`, which it does render. Still, the owner will open this page and see nothing.

The item title is drawn as an h4 that shows up as letter-spaced capitals "THING" (shot-2-after-tail.png, bottom band), so it reads like a section label, not a card. A thin `.live-item` frame (card look) would make it read as the item it is. No CSS was added for `.live-item`.

The page's own "Solution: a Ref" card (shot-1/2) still proposes the dropped `{"type":"Ref","file":…}` line. When the mastermind adds the real `items` line in the main tree, it should also update that card to the `{"items":{"add":{"file":"thing.jsonl"}}}` line.

Nothing in session.jsonl shows a run of `node Server/smoke.mjs` on /live/item-test/, which the brief requires. The new page_tools test also writes a temporary folder under public/framework/core/Item/. It cleans up in `finally`, but a crash mid-test leaves a stray folder in the site tree; os.tmpdir() with a mapped PUBLIC would be safer.

A fresh agent can continue from this folder: requirements-2.md says it replaces requirements.md, dropped-ref-file.patch is labelled reference-only, and the session.jsonl log names commit 99b037ff7, the test counts, and mastermind-live-page's review (its capture fix is already in the diff at LivePage.js:522).
